chase: Sweetheart, I can see your shadow on the tiles, and I'm not impressed.
Not so fast. I haven't finished adding up what you owe.
Left at the stairs, straight down to my counter. I'll wait.
I'll have you in the book before you reach the lift.
Round the corner, straight down, and you'll be right in my shop.
Still running? I'll put that on your tab, sweetheart.
Come on, the counter's just ahead. I'm not going anywhere.
I don't need to chase you, love. Every hallway ends at my till.
You're boxed in between my stall and the stairs, sweetheart.
Running in circles, are we? The till is still right here.
Keep moving, love. Every step adds to what you owe.
Don't stop now, sweetheart. The bill grows with every hall.
Close enough to smell the tea, sweetheart. Come on, then.
The counter is the only way out I'm offering, sweetheart.
You can't dodge a merchant who knows every corner, love.
Running in my shop, sweetheart? That's a fee.
Keep moving toward the till. I'll be right there.
The aisle is narrow, love. I'll catch you there.
catch: Got you, love. That deal went through whether you liked it or not.
Caught you lingering by the till. Browse all you like, but pay up.
Bad luck, sweetheart. Some deals are fair, and some are not.
Short on coins, sweetheart? You're coming with me, then.
A bad deal dragged you off. Read the board next time, sweetheart.
The deal took you, sweetheart. Nobody walks out of my shop empty.
Ledger says you're mine now, sweetheart. Sit down while we settle.
Hold still, sweetheart. I'll have the trade sorted in a moment.
You're taken for the bill, sweetheart. Don't argue with the till.
Got you, sweetheart. Next time, check the price board first.
Don't struggle, love. It's only a little trade gone wrong.
Oh dear, you walked straight into the trade. Lovely, though.
The coins are gone and so are you, sweetheart. Tough luck.
The bad deal has you now, sweetheart. Nothing personal, love.
That bad deal caught you fair and square, sweetheart.
Caught you! Hand over the change, sweetheart.
Got you, love. Settle up before you leave.
There we are, love. Shop's closed for you.
hear: That sounded like a dropped coin, sweetheart. Someone's near.
Somebody's rattling the stall shutter. Hello? Shop's open.
Footsteps by the stairs. Customer or trouble, I wonder.
A door just banged somewhere. Mind the crates, sweetheart.
Something broke over that way. Someone's paying for that.
A shout from the back rooms. Whose tab is that?
Heard a crash near the lift. Someone's been careless again.
That's a rattle of tins, sweetheart. Someone's raiding the tray.
Footsteps creeping by the counter. Shop's open, sweetheart. Come in.
Something dropped in the next hall. Let me check the ledger first.
I heard that door. Nobody goes in the back without paying.
Noise by the stairs again. I'm counting, so it can wait.
A bang and then silence. Silence always costs something, sweetheart.
Creak on the landing. Sweetheart, I can hear your boots from here.
Scraping near the vents. Nobody trades down there, sweetheart.
Coins rattled behind the counter. Hello, sweetheart?
A shelf fell by the window. Someone's pinching stock.
The door chime went off. Let's see who's in.
search: Lost you again, sweetheart. Shop's still open whenever you're ready.
Where did you go? The tea's getting cold, sweetheart.
I'll check the back rooms, then the stairs, then the stall.
You've slipped out of my sight. Everyone comes back to the till.
Gone quiet again? Quiet customers always owe the most.
Still hunting? I'll keep the kettle warm for you.
Nobody's at the counter now. Shame, I had a deal ready.
Lost sight of you. Walk back to my stall when you're done hiding.
Right, I'll update the ledger and wait for you to come back.
Gone off somewhere, have you? Fine. I'll be right here.
The shadows are thick tonight, sweetheart. You can't hide forever.
Where'd you get to? Don't make me count the whole house.
Searching is tiring, sweetheart. Have a cup of tea and we'll talk.
I'll look along the wall. You owe me a visit, sweetheart.
Too quiet down here. Come out, and we'll settle the bill.
stunned: Ow. Careful with that, sweetheart, that's my good china.
My hands are numb, sweetheart. Give me a moment.
That zap went straight through my tea tray. Rude.
Shaking it off, sweetheart. Don't think I'm finished.
My knees are shaking, sweetheart. Give me a minute to stand.
Right, my legs have gone funny. One moment, sweetheart.
Crowbar to the shoulder, and I'm still counting, sweetheart.
Easy with the axe, sweetheart. I'm getting my balance back.
Give me a second, love. My ledger fell and so did I.
Ouch. That's coming off your tab, sweetheart.
That's a rough way to get a discount. Very rough.
That taser buzz has me tingling all over, sweetheart.
I'm wobbling, but the till is still standing. Barely.
Ow, that stung. Put the weapon down before you make it worse.
Shaking the sting off now. I'll be right back at the counter.
hide_spot: Hiding in a locker? Bold choice, sweetheart. Rent's extra.
Checking under the bed? Every bed here has a price, sweetheart.
Hiding is free, sweetheart. Getting found costs a little more.
Hiding behind the crates? The tea stays warm, and so will I.
Lockers are for paying customers, sweetheart. Come out and pay.
Cozy in there? I'll put a fee on that cupboard, love.
Something's in the locker. Sweetheart, I can see your sleeve.
The bed is a poor hiding spot, sweetheart. Far too obvious.
I checked the locker and the cupboard. Both are on my books now.
Under the desk, is it? Lovely hideout, sweetheart. Still on my list.
Shelf space costs extra, sweetheart. Pay your way out of there.
A good hiding spot always costs something. Usually a tip.
I'll open the locker slowly. Please don't take a swing.
Pretty clever, tucking yourself away. My ledger still notices.
Cupboard's full, sweetheart. There isn't room for another customer.
light: Put that flashlight down, sweetheart, you're blinding the merchandise.
Shining that light on my stall is a fee, sweetheart.
Ow, that flashlight is right in my face, sweetheart.
Easy with that beam, love. My eyes are not made for light.
Turn that flashlight away, sweetheart. The stock is already wrapped.
All that glare and no purchase. Not a good look, sweetheart.
I can't see a thing, sweetheart. Point the flashlight at the floor.
Brighter than the price board, that flashlight. Shocking, sweetheart.
You've got the flashlight on my good stock. Lower it, sweetheart.
Careful, the glare is ruining my good shelves, sweetheart.
My ledger's gone blurry from that flashlight. Lower it, please.
Blinded by the beam, love. Give me a moment to read the price.
Such a bright flashlight for a little shop. Dim it, sweetheart.
Turn your flashlight away from the till, sweetheart. I can barely add.
Oh, that's bright! Sweetheart, I'm dazzled, and I'm not happy.
idle: The kettle's always on. Pull up a seat if you want one.
I count everything twice, once for me and once for the kettle.
The stalls go quiet in the dark. Honestly, I like the quiet.
Tray's full, sweetheart. Help yourself, but write your name down.
I leave a cup on the landing every night, with a saucer on top.
Eat something, sweetheart. You look like you skipped breakfast.
Tea first, then business. Tea helps the coins go down easier.
Who wants a cookie with their tea? Nobody? Fine, more for me.
Polishing the till again. It always needs a good shine.
Counting coins is restful, sweetheart. Like rain on a tin roof.
Another quiet hour, another ledger line. I'm content, sweetheart.
Rearranging the price tags again. They always drift, sweetheart.
Quiet hours are the best for stocktaking, sweetheart.
Dusting the scale and talking to the kettle. Nobody asked.
The cookie tin is nearly empty. I'm blaming the others.
ability: Coins in, trade done. Coins out, no refunds, sweetheart.
Pick a number from one to four, and I'll fix you up right away.
Some deals go sour. My prices are honest, but luck is not my department.
Every deal is fair, and some are only a little unlucky.
Walk up, look at the board, then choose. Choose wisely, love.
Read the price board first, sweetheart. A bad deal can still catch you.
Cool your nerves for a few coins. Cooling is my favorite trade.
Warm you up for a price, sweetheart. Cold feet never sell anything.
Repairs are cheap, usually. The lamp shines like new once paid.
Pesticide keeps the bugs away for a while. Pay now, scratch later.
Four offers on the board, sweetheart. Pick one and pay for it.
Cool, warm, repair, or pesticide. Which one are you buying, love?
Cooling and warming both cost coins, sweetheart. Choose carefully.
Coins can buy you a fixed lamp, sweetheart, if you have enough.
The trade is done the moment you pay, love. No second chances.
mechanic: Sabotaged relay? My repair offer can fix that, sweetheart. Coins, though.
Batteries are dear this week, sweetheart. Top up before you run.
The stairs are dark, sweetheart. Mind the third step down.
Vents are a rat run, sweetheart. I don't sell vent passes.
The shop door sticks when you slam it. Mind the hinge, love.
Radar pings bounce off my counter. Very annoying, sweetheart.
Items cost coins, sweetheart. Nothing in this shop is free.
A bad fall on the landing costs you, love. Watch the edge.
Relay's down again? Bring me the coins and I'll see to it.
The lift is out of order. Use the stairs and watch the coins.
Sabotage that relay and you'll be paying for it, love.
The door at the top of the stairs sticks. Give it a shove, sweetheart.
Vent grates rattle when someone sneaks through. I'd know, sweetheart.
Batteries cost more than tea, sweetheart. Plan your trips.
Those steps down are slippery near the till. Walk slowly, love.
Repair relay is behind the counter, love. Five coins.
Batteries are dear this week, so mind your power.
Relay panel's by the shutter. Mind the price.
